title: Compositor effect not called every frame
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4 and 4.5

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS 24.04 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (nvidia; 535.274.02) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6850K CPU @ 3.60GHz (12 threads) - 31.25 GiB memory

### Issue description

It seems that Godot does not render a frame if the scene does not change, so as a result when this happens compositor effect callbacks are not called. This is fine for static effects, but is problematic for time-dependent effects, as this mechanism freezes what the effects are supposed to compute every frame.

I believe this is not a bug but just how passive rendering works, but I am not able to find information about notifying RenderingServer that I want to render every frame / next frame.

### Steps to reproduce

MRP gives an example. In the editor, a script counts the number of callbacks and prints it every second. Ideally the count increases about 60 every second. But in reality we get only 1, and that is because the printing itself triggers another redraw. We may get a few more counts if we move the mouse around and touch the Editor GUI. Curiously, by running the project, not just by looking in the editor, we get 60 callbacks per second.

The callback count increases 1 or a few more per second.
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/155bd169-2274-4d7e-80c9-cfac2d887b44)

This is when I move a mesh instance a little bit every frame by script. I get around 60 callbacks per second, as expected.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39db967e-434b-472b-ba1f-74a7d853022f)



### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[compositor_callback.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23981125/compositor_callback.zip)
